samples.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This file bundles three essays. Kevin de Laplante reads Paul Chadwick's Concrete story 'Stay Tuned for Pearl Harbor', treating Concrete's angry monologue about oil companies and overpopulation as enlightened anthropocentrism, while Maureen's silent reverie of merging her body with root systems and being 'raped' by bulldozers dramatizes Arne Naess's deep-ecological expanded self and an ecofeminist link between the oppression of nature-as-female and of women; the utilitarianism of Bentham and Mill and Leopold's 'think like a mountain' land ethic frame the anthropocentrism/nonanthropocentrism debate. Pierre Skilling reads The Adventures of Tintin through Montesquieu's and Aristotle's typologies of government, casting Marshal Kurvi-Tasch's Borduria as Arendt-style totalitarianism (a secret police as true executive, a bid for world domination) against the legitimate monarchy of King Muskar XII, whose Syldavian sceptre works as a check on royal power. Terry Kading argues that 9/11 collapsed the superhero genre's binary of good versus evil into reality: bin Laden's 'monomaniacs' act as supervillains with a murky agenda, yet Spider-Man, Captain America and Superman comics concede no real superhero can rescue us, leaving only ordinary heroism and the compromised politics of national security.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: The Onion’s New Environmental Ethic
samples.relation: Matthew Altman reads Onion environmental satire as a staged escape from anthropocentrism: 'New, Delicious Species Discovered' and 'Beauty Of National Forest Enjoyed By Logger' expose that even appreciating nature is just valuing it for us, while the mascara-testing lab rabbit and 'Funny Monkey Tested On' make Singer's speciesism charge vivid against factory farming and animal experiments. He then widens the argument to a biocentric concern for species and ecosystems via 'Stuffed-Animal Biodiversity Rising' and 'Consumer-Product Diversity Now Exceeds Biodiversity,' and to ecofeminism via 'Raped Environment Led Polluters On,' where the forest as flirtatious woman links domination of nature to sexism and victim-blaming. Global stories like the Bush 'national air conditioner' piece show Western overconsumption displacing blame onto Third World overpopulation, and 'I'm Doing My Inconsequential Part' satirizes the self-satisfaction of green consumerism itself — leaving the measure of the Onion's philosophical importance as how dangerous it is.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: Tilting at Windmills
samples.relation: Reads Protogen through Horkheimer and Adorno's Dialectic of Enlightenment: like Odysseus tied to the mast while his sailors take the wax, Dresden's team had empathy surgically removed ('we modified our science team to remove ethical restraints'), Mao weeps at Julie's protomolecule corpse yet calls her death 'lucky', and Strickland experiments on Katoa and Mei Meng — self-made monsters serving the Baconian dream of conquering nature (New Atlantis, witch-trial language of 'penetrating her holes and corners'). Via Maria Mies and Carolyn Merchant's ecofeminism, it traces this domination of nature to pastoralist castration and the control of women's reproduction, culminating in Marco's theft of Filip and 'She left us. She left us both' — Naomi cast as nature to be mastered. Against them, Holden's childhood on the family farm, a cooperative 'let grow and make grow' world, is why Avasarala cannot play him and why he withholds broadcasts at Ilus: he is a knight who wants everyone to grow and speak for themselves, not to conquer.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bernard Rollin reads Dr. Zaius's tribunal as 'scientific ideology' in action - 'human see, human do' refuses to believe its own eyes, just as bishops refused to look through Galileo's telescope. He traces the ideology from Newton's 'hypotheses non fingo' through logical positivism's verifiability criterion (which validates the Hasslein Curve prediction while rendering 'there are intelligent beings in Heaven' meaningless) and Wittgenstein's point that 'killing is wrong' is not a fact of the universe, to the 'science is value-free' dogma that left animal pain untested and untreated - as he documents from his own campaign: the empty analgesic literature search, the 1985 federal legislation, and the pain physiologist whose dog research refutes his own denial. Zira's neurosurgery on mute humans repeats what Descartes's beast-machine doctrine licensed, and IASP's language requirement for pain collapses into a Cratylus-grade confusion of necessary and sufficient conditions ('You can't step into the same river once').

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 17. Life Unchecked Will Cease to Exist
samples.relation: Diego Perez Lasserre argues Thanos is not an external villain but a personification of what Heidegger and Carl Schmitt call the 'metaphysics of technology': once modernity banished transcendence from the metaphysical realm, mundane concepts like economic growth and pleasure occupied it, turning nature into mere resource (a tree becomes furniture or paper) until, as Descartes's mastering stance predicts, devouring the world leaves 'life unchecked' facing extinction. Read this way, the Snap is the inevitable consequence of our own predatory interpretation of the world, and the Avengers only prevail in Endgame once their existential crises evict growth-and-wealth concepts from their metaphysical realm, replacing them with family (Tony), friendship (Natasha), justice (Hawkeye), self-knowledge (Banner), love (Vision and Wanda), and transcendence (Rogers). The closing exchange, 'the arrogant never do' suspect a thing, is read as a warning about our own climate crisis.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: The Legend Has Come True. The Wind Has Come Back
samples.relation: Haas opposes two princesses of Nausicaa of the Valley of the Wind: Kushana of Tolmekia, whose 'whatever it takes' survivalism (invading Pejite, resurrecting a God-Warrior) is consequentialism pursued to its limit, and Nausicaa, whose attention to each act — befriending the biting fox-squirrel, staying her sword over her father's killer because vengeance would doom the Valley — restricts means, not just ends. The reductio comes from Pejite, whose torture of a baby Ohmu to bait a stampede on the Valley is exactly what strict outcome-maximization requires; against this, Kant's demand to treat beings as ends in themselves explains Nausicaa's 'mysterious power' of empathy. Because she respects the jungle and the sentient Ohmu rather than viewing nature anthropocentrically as a plague to burn, she discovers the plants are purifying the war-poisoned earth — the knowledge that saves everyone and proves Kushana's conquering approach self-defeating even on its own terms.

samples.book: 308 - The Palgrave Handbook of Popular Culture as Philosophy
samples.title: 34. The Lord of the Rings as Philosophy Environmental Enchantment and Resistance in Peter Jackson and J.R.R. T
samples.relation: Whitmire and Henderson read Peter Jackson's LotR films as environmental philosophy, arguing they use fantasy to recover a sense of nature's wonder and model a plurality of caring, non-instrumentalizing ways of inhabiting the land (Hobbits' gardens, the Rohirrim and their horses, the Elves of Lorien, the Ents of Fangorn) against the extractive, insatiable devastation of Saruman's Isengard and Sauron's Mordor. They explicitly deploy Leopold's Land Ethic ('the conqueror role is eventually self-defeating') to condemn Saruman's clear-cutting and dam-building, and Val Plumwood's ecofeminist notion of 'backgrounding' to explain why holding trees and mountains in visual focus is itself an argument. Thoreau's Maine Woods passage on the living pine grounds their claim that a tree is more than lumber, and the film's resistance (the Ents tearing out the dam, the White Tree's bloom) is read as a call to active ecological hope.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Jeff Ewing reads Victor's science through ecofeminist and Marxist critiques: M. Waldman's promise to 'penetrate into the recesses of nature' and 'show how she works in her hiding-places' exemplifies exactly what Val Plumwood condemns - male knowers wringing secrets from a nature pictured as a passive female slave - and Victor studies natural elements 'in their death, not in their life' as raw material for power. Marx and Engels supply the parallel diagnosis: capitalism biases science and technology toward profit, turning tools and knowledge into means of domination rather than human flourishing, just as Victor's knowledge serves only his glory and kills everyone he loves. The chapter concludes that we breed Frankenstein's monsters whenever science treats nature, workers, women, and othered peoples as mere instruments, and only replacing those social relations frees science from power and profit.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Roger Hunt answers 'what do philosophers do?' through Dennis's seduction methodology. Frank embodies empiricism, leaving the comfort of principle for the messiness of the world as Hume did when he found no impression of causation, space, or time; Mac embodies rationalism, reasoning with total confidence from a principle he cannot doubt, as Descartes did from the cogito; and the dialectic of Socrates and Plato, questioning beliefs in dialogue to see what survives scrutiny, describes philosophy as it is actually practiced. Boethius's Consolation - the imprisoned author consoled by dialogues with Lady Philosophy - supplies the frame of philosophy as an encounter with a woman one pursues, and each D.E.N.N.I.S. step maps onto the craft: Demonstrating value to the problem, Engaging physically in its awkward grind, Nurturing dependence through thesis panic, Neglect and Inspiring hope on the road to the defense, then Separating entirely - 'be a sociopath about it.'

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 8. Time Travel and the Problem of Evil
samples.relation: Ray Bossert reads Endgame through Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy, arguing that Doctor Strange and Tony Stark, who permit the Snap and five years of suffering for the sake of the one winning outcome, run 'uncannily parallel' to Thanos, who decided for Gamora that her unwilling death served the greater good. Strange's viewing of 14,000,605 futures illustrates Boethius's distinction between an infinite being riding along the timeline and an eternal one seeing all moments at once, and the refusal to tell Stark his role mirrors why God's foreknowledge sees our choices without compelling them. Boethius's providence weaving free choices into justice, the Avengers' passion-driven failures on Titan (Star-Lord and Thor avenging lost lovers), justice as the wicked's own punishment (Thanos dying wretched twice in one film), and Umberto Eco's 'Myth of Superman' all frame a universe where suffering is allowed because it is woven into a pattern that ends in justice.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a19.xhtml
samples.relation: Sterling takes Gandalf's 'Bilbo was meant to find the Ring, and not by its maker' as a claim of providence by Eru Iluvatar, which generates the problem of divine foreknowledge: if Eru arranged for the Ring to slip from Gollum's grasp, he must have foreknown countless free choices (Bilbo choosing to follow, Dori carrying him, Gollum strangling the goblin whimper-pip). Open theism's open future fails because Tolkien's Music of the Ainur prefigures all things except the free will of Elves and Men, and compatibilist escapes (Hobbes, Hume, Frankfurt, Dennett) are dismissed as inadequate. The solution is Boethius' Consolation of Philosophy: Eru is outside time, beholding all events in an eternal present - like holding the whole film reel at once - so his 'foreknowledge' is timeless vision, and Tolkien's 'Osanwe-kenta' confirms that minds in Time cannot see the future except through Eru.

samples.book: 156 - Dune and Philosophy - Minds, Monads, and Muad'Dib
samples.title: Intending the Way Out
samples.relation: Works through the paradox of foreknowledge: because Paul's Caladan dream of first meeting Chani is knowledge in Plato's justified-true-belief sense, the foreseen future is factive, so his struggle against the jihad he visions (even hoping to die on Feyd-Rautha's blade rather than become a martyr) is futile. It tests the classical escape routes, Boethius's God who views all times as an ever-present eternity and Aquinas's God seeing the whole road 'under the aspect of eternity', and Laplace's Demon's causal determinism, but finds the Atreides oracles unlike God since they are creatures in time who see many possible futures rather than one. The resolution comes through Anscombe's Intention: practical knowledge lets Paul and Leto, whose present choices shift the balance of probability among foreseen timelines, intend their way out as creative authors of events.

samples.book: 017 - Bob Dylan and Philosophy - It's Alright Ma (I'm Only Thinking)
samples.title: “The Foggy Ruins of Time”
samples.relation: Kevin Stoehr stages Plato's ancient quarrel between philosophy and poetry over Dylan: from the Republic's banishment of the poets, through Boethius's Consolation where Lady Philosophy banishes the Muses yet the book stays a prose-poem satura, to Nietzsche, who attacks philosophy philosophically just as Dylan discounts thinking while waxing philosophical about it. Dylan's own remarks ("the song wrote itself," "trust my intuition") side with poetic intuition against analysis, and Holderlin's question "what are poets for in a destitute time" frames Dylan as the smirking antiquary of a nihilistic age who makes us feel the darkness philosophy can only point at. The chapter concludes that the ambiguity of songs like "Lay, Lady, Lay" resists universalization yet occasions the wonder in which philosophy begins - poetry as the bridge to philosophy.

samples.book: 005 - The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy - One Book to Rule Them All
samples.title: The Lord of the Rings and Philosophy
samples.relation: John Davenport argues that The Lord of the Rings is neither mere adventure nor Christian allegory but an epic fairy tale whose 'eucatastrophe' - Tolkien's term for the sudden joyous turn, a miraculous reprieve - carries religious hope even though the book contains no churches or prayers. Drawing on Tolkien's 'On Fairy-stories', he makes Sir Gawain and the Green Knight the model for Frodo: Gawain accepts the girdle and is scarred yet reprieved, just as Frodo claims the Ring, loses a finger as Beren lost a hand, and is saved only because the mercy shown Gollum lets the Ring fall into the fire. Gandalf's return, Éowyn's healing, and the sapling of Nimloth extend the pattern; with Kierkegaard the deliverance is grace 'by virtue of the absurd', an echo of the eschaton answering Boethius's question whether our struggles have final significance.

samples.book: 083 - The Devil and Philosophy - The Nature of His Game
samples.title: The Devil and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ray Bossert reads Tolkien's Silmarillion through Boethius's Consolation of Philosophy: elves, being artists, understand Melkor not as tempter but as bad artist, from his rebellious solo in the Music of the Ainur to his botched sub-creations - orcs bred from kidnapped elves - and his covetous collecting of the silmarils. Boethius supplies the machinery: evil seeks a good by unnatural means and only approximates it, wickedness debases its practitioner into a beast, God's foreknowledge embraces free choices without causing them, and Providence is a spinning disc at whose center alone one is steady - so Melkor's rebellion leaves him less free, dragged around the rim. Tolkien's contrast between art (for beauty) and magic (for control) explains why the Devil can only mimic creation, never make anything real.

samples.book: 056 - Dune and Philosophy - Weirding Way of the Mentat
samples.title: Intending the Way Out
samples.relation: Stages the paradox of foreknowledge through Paul's prescient dream of meeting Chani and his futile struggle against the foreseen jihad: since knowledge (on Plato's justified-true-belief account) is factive, a known future seems unalterable. It tests the classic escapes—Boethius's God in ever-present eternity and Aquinas's seeing all time 'under the aspect of eternity,' Laplace's demon, Richard Taylor's fatalism—and finds the Atreides oracles are no gods, only probabilistic predictors whose visions fix the possibilities they see. The way out is Anscombe's Intention: like God knowing creation because He authored it, Paul and Leto know their futures practically, as agents whose intentions help decide which possibilities become actual, so freedom survives as terrific responsibility.

samples.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
samples.title: What’s Wrong with Generalization
samples.relation: Brannigan uses Japanese baseball to ask what is wrong with cultural generalization. He presents the Bushido case — samurai-style self-denial, absolute loyalty (Kawakami's Yomiuri Giants), Suisha Tobita's 'training of death,' resolve (konjo), team harmony (wa), and a relational self grounded in Buddhism's no-self and Confucian identity-through-relationships — then tests it against counter-evidence: Sadaharu Oh's flamingo swing owed as much to individual talent and Hiroshi Arakawa's unconventional kendo-and-aikido coaching as to sensei imitation, the 'new breed' (Ochiai, Egawa) flouts the old ways, and William Kelly's 'Whiting problem' warns against polarizing Japanese and American baseball. The chapter's 'three strikes' against the label 'Japanese baseball' conclude that generalizations become dangerous when treated as monolithic nets cast over an entire culture.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 14. When the Stakes Are Highest
samples.relation: John Karavitis argues the Infinity War-Endgame arc only makes sense through the alien lens of feudal Japan's warrior code as codified in Yamamoto Tsunetomo's Hagakure, where 'the way of the warrior is to be found in dying' and success is measured in death, the enemy's and one's own. He reads Thanos's sacrifice of Gamora, his calm acceptance of death in the Garden, Black Widow's and Tony's willing sacrifices, and Thor's failure to 'go for the head' at Wakanda through Olivier Ansart's concepts of ichinen (single-minded resolve) and shini-gurui (the frenzy to die), with the code's roots in Buddhism, Shinto, and Confucianism. The provocation is that Thanos, not the fractious Avengers, is the true samurai, since his voluntary destruction of the Infinity Stones shows the self-discipline the code demands.

samples.book: 029 - Quentin Tarantino and Philosophy - How to Philosophize with a Pair of Pliers and a Blowtorch
samples.title: Are We Going Too Far
samples.relation: David Kyle Johnson distinguishes revenge (personal, emotional, unlimited) from retribution and argues that 'Tarantino's view'—mercy should be common practice yet revenge can be justified—is consistent: Jules buys Pumpkin and Honey Bunny's lives but never waives a right of vengeance, since they never wronged him. He tests the view against Bushido, showing Beatrix's revolt against her lord Bill violates the samurai code, and against karma, which makes revenge unnecessary. After finding that Hobbes, Locke, Nietzsche and Socrates all leave revenge's justification open, he defends it—citing Budd's 'that woman deserves her revenge'—so long as the punishment fits the crime and spares innocents, as when Beatrix refuses to make herself even by killing Vernita's daughter Nikki.

samples.book: 207 - Wonder Woman and Philosophy - The Amazonian Mystique
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Bein argues Wonder Woman uniquely fuses two supposedly incompatible moralities: bushido - Nitobe's eight samurai virtues, Sun Tzu's benevolence of ending war swiftly, worthy-opponent rituals mirrored in superhero costumes - and the feminist ethics of care Gilligan and Noddings built against a Western canon (Aristotle, Kant) that called women too emotional for morality. Wonder Woman's killing of Maxwell Lord to free Superman is re-read as the care-ethical beach case: saving your own child over a stranger's is not a failure of impartiality, and in his Gotham-versus-Themyscira invasion thought experiment she would defend Gotham because its people are vulnerable non-combatants, not because a utilitarian ledger favors it.

samples.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Baldwin argues the popular view of Bushido as a moral code (Nitobe, Star Wars, Kurosawa, Campbell's Jungian hero archetype) is historically wrong: by the Hagakure, Bushido is a death-ready 'mode of action' so morally neutral that even villains like Takezo Kensei or Sylar can practice it. He traces Hiro's evolution from comic-book and video-game hero-worship, through the Yaeko betrayal that turned Kensei into Adam Monroe, toward the fearless Future Hiro ideal of 'no-mind' readiness for death (echoing D.T. Suzuki's Zen reading). Because the Meiji reforms abolished the samurai class, Hiro can never literally be a samurai, only follow Bushido analogically, which lets him remain both superhero and samurai.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: No Way Out
samples.relation: Leah Murray argues Romero's Dead films stage the American contest between individualism and communitarianism inside the social contract: in Night of the Living Dead, communitarian Ben barricading the farmhouse against every-man-for-himself Mr. Cooper hiding in the basement; in Dawn of the Dead, the Peter-Roger-Fran-Stephen mall commune collapsing when Stephen's 'it's ours, we took it' meets the bikers; in Day of the Dead, Sarah's compassion against the racist, harassing soldiers; in Land of the Dead, Kaufman's Fiddler's Green as a Hobbesian Leviathan born of fear, complete with bread-and-circuses for the poor. Against the Hobbesian fear-born contract (Dawn opens in a full state-of-nature collapse) she sets Rousseau's general will and Tocqueville's civic association, embodied in Riley's freely formed community and in Big Daddy's zombies, who organize, turn from eating humans, and bring down the Leviathan. The films' verdict: fear-based individualist contracts collapse under their own contradictions, while compassionate cooperation — even among the Undead — is the only way out, even if Romero doubts its ultimate viability.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: So Why Do I Support Aston Villa
samples.relation: Rose—made a Villan by misreading a 1978 Panini sticker as Aston Villa's claret and blue—asks whether supporting Aston Villa is rational and argues ethics is far more like fandom than philosophers admit. Reasons for supporting Villa (local team, the 1982 European Cup, the colors) explain but never justify his allegiance, and the impartial procedures ethics prizes—the utilitarian benevolent spectator and Rawls's original position behind the veil of ignorance, with its 'sort of Kantian' consent-based alternative—turn out too demanding and too abstract: they would force him to donate his match ticket to charity, forbid the Premiership manager favoring his academy son, and reduce agency to the 'Rose-calcio scale' absurdity of switching to Real Madrid for rational reasons. His positive, communitarian claim is that we are thrown into social traditions whose inherited values—like a team—make moral agency and action possible at all, a 'different kind of rationality' that flirts with relativism yet still needs an exit strategy for cultures that discriminate against women or torture children.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: 16 - Quantitative and Qualitative Change
samples.relation: This edited LibriVox podcast transcript catches three volunteers debating free culture: Wittkower argues copyright is an artificial monopoly justified only when printing presses made reproducing texts capital-intensive — now that consumer gear has put industrial-scale production in everyone's basement ('the working man has wrested the means of production from the big man'), a thirteen-year-old should be free to strip vocals and remix her culture. McGaughey's title thesis — cheap technology means a quantitative change becomes a qualitative change, 'which is by the way from Hegel's Logic' — answers Mowatt's deflation that the Internet merely lowers the bar for things you could always have done locally. Connecting Putnam's Bowling Alone decline of social trust to narrow-casting as a way of rebuilding communities of common concern, they hold up LibriVox's 1,668 free public-domain audiobooks (327 days of audio, volunteers on six continents) as a gift-economy counter-model to a culture we only 'rent' as serfs on branded soil.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: No Way Out
samples.relation: Leah Murray reads Romero's Dead series as an argument about the American social contract, individualism versus communitarianism. Night of the Living Dead's farmhouse is Hobbes: fear throws strangers Ben and Mr. Cooper into a makeshift commonwealth whose individualist half ('every man for himself' in the basement) fails, while Dawn shows the Hobbesian next step - martial law as Leviathan - after the state of nature returns. Land of the Dead's Fiddler's Green is a fear-born contract corrupting into Kaufman's hierarchy, and Big Daddy's zombies form the counter-model, a Rousseauian community of the general will based on mutual bonds rather than terror, as the priest in Dawn already urged ('we must stop the killing... or lose the war'). Following Tocqueville on civic association, she concludes Romero's survivors - Ben, Peter, Sarah, Riley - vindicate communitarian cooperation, even though Night's bureaucratic ending suggests there may be no way out.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: Wonder Why We Ever Go Home
samples.relation: Duke Richey maps Buffett's West — 'Ringling, Ringling,' the Rancho Deluxe soundtrack, Tully Mars — onto Josiah Royce's philosophy of community: only people who root in a place, face its history ('wise provincialism'), and sacrifice selfish desires for the whole can build Beloved Communities, a lesson enacted when cattle rustlers Jack and Cecil accept community sanction and find belonging working the Rancho Deluxe. Wallace Stegner's coral-reef metaphor from Angle of Repose supplies the image of communities built up millimeter by millimeter yet still vulnerable to pollution and over-fishing, with Royce's environmental regret (covering 'the wounds' of the landscape with gardens) anticipating the chapter's sustainability ethic. 'Wonder Why We Ever Go Home' thus asks what we really seek when we seek grace through community: not the nomadic Pickup Truck Death of every-man-for-himself, but cooperation that makes a society to match the scenery.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Mike Kugler argues Shelley's novel tests the radical idealism of her father William Godwin, her mother Mary Wollstonecraft, and her husband Percy: Victor's Promethean project of perfecting humanity in isolation, away from the 'intimate circle' of family and friends, produces a creature whose natural benevolence is destroyed only by repeated exclusion, first by the De Laceys. Drawing on Rousseau's and Wollstonecraft's view that children raised by benevolent parents develop their innate sympathy, the chapter reads the creature as an abandoned child - a new Adam who becomes a Satanic rebel when every community rejects him - and Victor's attempt at reproduction without women and mothers as the novel's deepest violation. The redemptive counterfactual is adoption: what if Victor had raised the creature in his home, as his father did Elizabeth?

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: You Can Go Home Again
samples.relation: Fortune stages the movie as a morality play between two conceptions of personhood: the Wizard is an atomist, a self-sufficient ball from the Chuck E. Cheese ball pit who is the same humbug in Omaha or Oz and who reduces heart, brains, and courage to a testimonial, a diploma, and a medal, while Dorothy is a relationalist, a pineapple chunk that belongs on one particular pizza, a person constituted by her web of relations to home. 'There's no place like home' is therefore the relationalist's slogan, an acceptance of home for everything it is, good and bad, with Toto's fate still unresolved under Miss Gulch's law. He closes by suggesting the film's delayed television-era triumph is existential nostalgia: modern, rootless, ear-budded Americans keep watching because the relationalist country it mourns is 'what's in our blood.'

samples.book: 016 - Hip-Hop and Philosophy - Rhyme 2 Reason
samples.title: Reality versus Revolution
samples.relation: McPherson argues political rap has never been politically revolutionary, sorting it into three schools: the amoral "gangsta Hobbes" ethic (Mobb Deep's "Survival of the Fittest", 50 Cent's "get rich or die tryin'") that sees the hood as Hobbes's state of nature where no social contract with blacks ever existed; Afrocentric communitarianism, split between nationalist separatists (Brand Nubian, X-Clan, Dead Prez) and the more cosmopolitan Native Tongues (De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest); and a radical liberalism closer to Rawls than its adherents admit. Against Chuck D's "What's a smilin' face when the whole state's racist?", he argues Rawls's original position, veil of ignorance, and difference principle - applied with real-world knowledge of racism - support rather than oppose Public Enemy's demands for racial justice.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: A Little bit of Messi for our Life
samples.relation: The authors cast the contrast between disciplined European and improvisational South American football as Mill's struggle between liberty and authority: the coach's tactical orders are 'rules of opinion' the genius may defy, as Maradona did on his sixty-meter run to the Goal of the Century, while the harm principle marks the line at the 'rules of law' — FIFA's Laws of the Game. The Hand of God goal, which broke even a rule of law yet stood because 'a goal is scored when the referee says so', illustrates Searle's point that football's regulative capacity cannot guarantee its agreements, leaving a gap filled only by ethics and fair play. Following Wittgenstein's 'ethics and aesthetics are one and the same', they conclude that a bit of Messi-style rule-breaking — Messi replicated both Maradona goals in 2007 — is what makes football, and life, joyful and beautiful.

samples.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
samples.title: The Basket That Never Was
samples.relation: Thomas Flint's thought experiment - a conference-championship buzzer-beater waved off because the clock expired, with inconclusive video - asks whether South Shore 'really' scored. He rejects the 'Goofy View' that game facts are referee-independent, since it would entail that only he and his camcorder-owning boss know who won any game ever (imperiling even Michael Jordan's 1982 title and Pistol Pete's scoring record) and would poison a coach's duty to teach rule-following when officials miss traveling. He also rejects the 'Tyranny of the Zebras' that makes officials infallible like the pope, since NCAA replay rules presuppose fallibility, and settles on officials as contest judges who award points: without the verdict no points exist, yet a blown call remains a genuine mistake in failing to apply the rules properly.

samples.book: 006 - Baseball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Batter's Box
samples.title: The Ambiguous Consolations of Philosophy
samples.relation: Ted Cohen shows that 'ties go to the runner' is no convention but follows from Rule 6.05(j) (the runner is out only if tagged before he touches first), then discovers that Rule 7.08(e) contradicts 6.05(j) once 6.09(a) makes a batter who hits a fair ball a runner: on a tie at first the rules say both out and safe. His letters to the National League rules committee get a polite brush-off ('there never are any ties'), and the essay meditates on how players barely know the rules (the 2000 World Series third-strike misplay, cricket's time-wasting law, the spitball rule's gaps) and how rules written 'by journeymen lawyers' charm yet fail. Philosophy's consolation is ambiguous: knowing the rules cost him his teammates' respect, who 'knew the game in some other way.'

samples.book: 171 - House of Cards and Philosophy - Underwood's Republic
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Shea argues the Underwoods' rise is structurally guaranteed rather than far-fetched, surveying democracy's critics: Plato's Republic Books 8-9 has the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decay through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, where a 'protector'-tyrant like Frank exploits the drones and the people's love of freedom (Russo as the prototypical democratic soul, Tusk as the oligarch-in-fact), while the tyrant ends fear-ridden and friendless — precisely Frank's Season 3. Hobbes and Hegel then reverse the verdict, arguing monarchy aligns the ruler's private interest with the public good and lets a people will as one instead of a formless mass — the insight Tom Yates has about voters identifying with the Underwoods as people — and Marx reframes it economically: SanCorp, Tusk, and Feng are the capitalist structure, and Frank's AmWorks, entitlement cuts, and nationalization threats show self-interested politicians siding with a growing proletariat. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government supplies the democratic reply — responsiveness, better information, and citizen participation mean an Underwood cannot last if we keep fair elections, a free press, and real checks.

samples.book: 170 - House and Philosophy - Everybody Lies
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues the Underwoods' success is not far-fetched fiction but the structural outcome four critics of democracy predict. Plato's Republic supplies the spine: the kallipolis of philosopher-guardians decays through timocracy and oligarchy into democracy, whose love of freedom invites the tyrant — Peter Russo with his random desires is the democratic soul, Frank the tyrannical soul ruled by one illicit appetite, doomed to the fear and friendlessness Book 9 describes (which Season 3 delivers). Hobbes and Hegel then explain why monarchy may beat popular rule (the monarch's private interest aligns with the public's; the monarch lets a people will as one), and Marx reframes the whole show economically — SanCorp, Tusk and Feng as capitalists, the laid-off shipyard workers as proletariat, and AmWorks as self-interested politicians flirting with expropriation. Against all four, Mill's Considerations on Representative Government gives the democratic reply — elections force responsiveness, participation educates citizens — so the burden falls on viewers to keep elections fair, the press free, and checks on unscrupulous politicians effective.

samples.book: 065 - Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy - The Real and the Cereal
samples.title: Chuck Klosterman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Sienkiewicz argues that Klosterman's LeBron James 'Decision' episode on Bill Simmons's B.S. Report modeled genuine public-sphere deliberation: where ESPN's Skip Bayless scored points over whether James looked remorseful, Klosterman proposed, via Tupac's 'Only God can judge me', that the televised announcement was a statement of confidence and a refusal to play the one-dimensional reality-TV role America demanded. The chapter lays out Habermas's eighteenth-century public sphere, its salons and 'public sphere of letters' where low-stakes aesthetic arguments (Mozart then, the Guns N' Roses tribute band Paradise City now) train disinterested rational debate, and concedes Habermas's golden age is idealized historical fiction much like a Klosterman hyperthetical. Though Habermas blames commercial media for corroding rational discourse, Sienkiewicz contends that long-form podcasts like The B.S. Report and Contexts give Klosterman's pop-culture arguments the time and independence the old salons had, so arguing about Billy Joel or Ace Frehley strengthens rather than absolves democratic culture.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Charts Star Trek's handling of secularization, from the "Roddenberry attitude" of Kirk confronting fifteen would-be gods to later series' complications, using Robert Audi's nine features of religion and Benedict Anderson's "imagined community" - the Yangs' sacred flag and worship-word "freedom" in "The Omega Glory" show an incoherent civic religion Kirk can correct. "Who Watches the Watchers" inverts the dynamic by making Picard an accidental god who refuses to found a religion among the proto-Vulcan Mintakans, while real-world creationism in schools and abstinence-only sex education supply the chapter's empirical moral arguments that faith-driven public policy fails on its own terms. DS9's Bajor arc - Vedek Winn boycotting Keiko's school, Sisko's defense of the faith that sustained Bajor through occupation, and Akorem's restoration of the D'jarra castes in "Accession", likened to Plato's Republic-class soul hierarchy - grounds the claim that infallible religious authority corrodes democratic equality, with Sisko as the Emissary who synthesizes faith and secular governance.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Andrea Conque argues the adult-free ('Mungo-free') children of Little Lamplight are genuinely political: they socialize each other into distrust of grownups (mandatory exile at 16 to Big Town), elect mayors by secret popular vote - MacCready's punch against Princess was a coup made legitimate by subsequent election - and fill every office from doctor Lucy to teacher Joseph to Knock Knock, whose Vault Boy jokes 'keep the peace' against social isolation. Sherif's Robber's Cave experiment supplies the comparison: unlike the Eagles and Rattlers, Lamplighters avoid in-group conflict because the radiation-absorbing cave fungus and shared survival give them permanent superordinate goals, while Biwwy's high-damage 'wazer wifle' shows they deter oppression by being, not just posturing as, tough. Against MacCready's claim of 'pure anarchy', the chapter concludes Little Lamplight is the Capital Wasteland's most successful government - freer and better ordered than Megaton, Andale, Paradise Falls, or even the Republic of Dave.

samples.book: 116 - 1984 and Philosophy - Is Resistance Futile
samples.title: 24. Post-Factual Democracy
samples.relation: Hendricks and Vestergaard open with Trump's inauguration lies and Kellyanne Conway's 'alternative facts' to define post-factual democracy: a state in which opportune political narratives replace facts and evidence as the basis of debate, opinion formation and policymaking. Unlike Machiavelli, who taught that lies must at least be concealed, the post-factual politician pays no price for exposed falsehood once social media, the attention economy and populist us-versus-them narratives engineered for indignation and fear have stripped journalists and fact-checkers of authority — Arendt's remark that mass leaders show 'extreme contempt for facts as such' before fitting reality to their lies. Using Habermas's deliberative model and even minimal accountability theories of voting, they argue post-factuality destroys democratic legitimacy, and defend a 'factual democracy' that trusts science and journalism without becoming a technocracy — the real-world echo of the Party's command to reject the evidence of your eyes.

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter reads Salander's hacking beside Julian Assange's WikiLeaks: both are hard to classify as criminal or activist, and both live by the hacker ethic Stephen Levy codified—unlimited access, all information free, mistrust authority, judgment by skill—which later versions soften with privacy and social responsibility, matching 'Salander's Principles' (a bastard is always a bastard) and Assange's 'capable, generous men do not create victims; they nurture victims.' Through David Brin's Transparent Society it asks who watches the watchers—the police-camera city of the state or the citizen-accessible city—and argues for WikiLeaks-style reciprocal transparency that keeps the 'mighty' (governments, the Vanger Corporation, Wennerström) exposed while protecting whistleblower anonymity. Blomkvist's choices—suppressing the Vanger murders, encouraging Salander to steal Wennerström's files, planting disinformation—mark him as the journalist half of Larsson's new information-age hero pair.

samples.book: 094 - Divergent and Philosophy - The Factions of Life
samples.title: 8. Plato’s Chicago
samples.relation: Littmann systematically maps Roth's Chicago onto Plato's Republic: like Marcus, Plato rejects democracy after Athens executed Socrates; both dissolve the family ('faction before blood' versus children raised in common and bred by state schedule); Erudite's IQ-selected leadership mirrors the rigorously trained philosopher-rulers, Dauntless the warrior class whose purely physical training Plato warns turns 'savage and harsh,' Abnegation's poverty the guardians's communism of property, and the factionless the powerless producers - with Plato's noble lie about the metals matching the Erudite's propaganda and serums as instruments of control. The shared flaw, he argues, is concentrated power without external checks, which corrupted Abnegation, corrupts every Dauntless leadership change, and would corrupt Plato's guardians too. The lesson is not to hand power to the least vicious but for democratic voters to confront their own ignorance - or end like Roth's America, in apocalyptic war.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase Five' puzzle essays. Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro use Secret Wars to test omnipotence: the Beyonder, Doom, and Galactus cannot do the logically impossible (no spherical cubes, no stone too heavy to lift), two omnipotent beings collide, and a truly omnipotent being has no desires - so villains can never climb to the top they crave. Matthewson and Wall use Frankfurt cases and reasons-responsive source compatibilism to explain why Eddie Brock is responsible for Venom's villainy (he voluntarily bonded and endorses the symbiote's adjusted psychology) while Anne Weying, horrified by what the symbiote made her do, bears only minimal blame. Pickavance reconstructs the Ship of Theseus with Sandman's 'mansand': combining part exchange with materialism lets Norman Osborn reassemble a duplicate Sandman from his scattered remains, and since neither principle nor soul-dualism comes free, personal identity through material change remains unsolved. Loader argues Brainiac's reinvention as a 'facts and logic' computer embodies disembodied Cartesian AI, so the frame problem (Dennett's exploding robots) and embodied cognition (Clark's Tetris, Dreyfus) suggest his detachment from body and world would make him less, not more, intelligent than the humans he scorns.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: David Lawrence opens with Fallout 4's 'Blind Betrayal', where Elder Maxson orders the player to execute Paladin Danse once his synth origin is revealed, and argues that moral status is a matter of capacities - sense of self, notion of past and future, values, life-plans, moral agency - drawing on Charles Taylor's concept of a person and narrative identity, not on biological substrate. Nick Valentine's hunt for Eddie Winter in 'Long Time Coming' and Curie's chosen embodiment in 'Emergent Behavior' show machines weaving reconstructed pasts into new life-plans, while ghouls like Hancock and Raul ('Old School Ghoul') and super mutants like Fawkes (who refuses to enter the lethal radiation chamber: 'I would not rob you of that') and the community-builder Marcus prove branded monsters can be more human than human. The factions embody warring philosophies of moral status: the Institute's property-slavery of its creations, the Brotherhood's 'wisdom of repugnance' (Leon Kass), and the Railroad's capacity-based abolitionism, with DiMA's Far Harbor question - how do you know you are not a synth? - turning the issue on the player.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: The Loneliness of the Goalkeeper (Again)
samples.relation: Winters celebrates the goalkeeper's fingertip save—Gordon Banks denying Pelé's header in 1970—as football's aesthetic summit, reading the keeper as the lonely, 'stark mad' outsider of existentialist fiction, a lineage he anchors in Camus, the goalkeeper of Algiers who said all he knew of morality he learnt from football. Kant supplies both the dove of the first Critique—needing the air's resistance, just as the tango's strict steps enable the dancer's personality—and the target of critique: against Kantian disinterested contemplation, he adopts Graham's Nietzschean, Dionysiac aesthetics of participation, so spectators proprioceptively feel the keeper twisting in mid-air, as Wittgenstein's question about the galloping horse picture suggests the movement enters our muscles and joints. Understanding a save or a back-heel means seeing it under a general type ('that' free kick, 'that' volley, from Beckham at Wembley back to Garrincha), and Bloch's ruminations in Handke's The Goalie's Anxiety at the Penalty Kick show the keeper alone at the liminal limit where concession and prevention meet.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Nightmares
samples.relation: Auxier asks why the flying monkeys and the shriveling feet of the Wicked Witch of the East give children lifelong nightmares, and answers with a phenomenology of three frightening sequences in escalating duration: the instant shriveling shot, the five-minute cyclone (paired with 'The Great Gig in the Sky' in the Dark Side of the Rainbow sync), and the monkey air-raid. Kierkegaard's Concept of Anxiety supplies the depth psychology: innocence is ignorance, and the child's dreaming spirit projects its own nothing outward, fastening fear onto figures like the monkeys (who are, he notes, played by the Munchkin actors themselves). Merleau-Ponty's lived body versus habit body explains the mechanics: cinema seizes the body's usual 'tour of inspection,' Fleming manipulates active and passive synthesis (the scoreless build-up to the window blow, the barely noticed arsenal of weapons in the Haunted Forest, the dimming lights), and children construct a rigid, inescapable habit body within a single viewing, so the nightmare is the monkey inside our own projected world.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: The Transforming Body
samples.relation: McBlane reads Oshii's Ghost in the Shell as staging the collision between a humanist framework — Cartesian ghost-in-shell dualism where consciousness is the seat of identity — and a posthuman 'mindbody' of distributed cognition in which the body is an informational circuit extending into the net, so a data body is still a body. Motoko's crisis (is the real me the organic brain, the ghost, or nothing?) deepens through the hacked garbage-truck man ('There's nothing sadder than a puppet without a ghost') and resolves only in her fusion with the Puppet Master, whose line 'Your effort to remain what you are is what limits you' enacts the shift from one ghost to multiple, distributed subjectivities ending in a little girl's body with 'The net is vast.' Heidegger's Dasein and being-in-the-world supply the claim that access to Being expands beyond the human into technological and informational modes, while the film's angelic transcendence imagery shows how residual humanist mind-body splits persist even in a posthuman story.

samples.book: 147 - Bioshock and Philosophy - Irrational Game, Rational Book
samples.title: Is a Man Not Entitled to the Sweat of His Brow
samples.relation: Schevelier uses the Andrew Ryan assassination to teach phenomenology: the moment the controller stops responding, the 'mineness' of the experience collapses and the story stops being yours, revealing that Jack's (and the player's) freedom depended on a thin self-narrative the mind 'desperately struggles to create', per Lutece's epigraph. Nagel's bat shows why no brain scan captures what it is like to play, while Husserl, Heidegger, and Merleau-Ponty supply the toolkit; Heidegger's hammer, which shows itself in use or in breakdown, explains both immersive scenes like the Kashmir restaurant and what breaks them (bugs, wrong display, a talking protagonist). Following Merleau-Ponty's claim that art records subjective experience, the chapter treats Levine's team as artistic phenomenologists whose design question 'What is this experience we are trying to make?' turned Columbia and Elizabeth into phenomenological analyses to be read.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Knives Out
samples.relation: Michael Thompson argues that the much-debated rhythm of "Pyramid Song" — 4/4 with syncopation, 3/3/4/3/3 groupings, or shifting signatures; Yorke says it is only "felt" — is philosophically pointed: by violating ordinary temporal expectations it forces an awareness of time itself, just as Chopin's nocturnes used time-signature changes to voice the nostalgia and melancholy of his Polish exile. Drawing on Gadamer's historically affected consciousness and the embodied, rhythmic daily life described by Heidegger and Merleau-Ponty, he reads the lyrics' row-boat to heaven ("all my past and futures") as a synoptic flash in which one sees past, present, and future as one organic whole. Because Yorke's heaven echoes Talking Heads' "Heaven" as a place where nothing happens, the song's consolation is that nothing lies outside our temporal embedding — with past and future united "there was nothing to fear and nothing to doubt."

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Argues Star Trek functions like the Greek myths Nussbaum describes: modern tales of transformation (Gary Mitchell in "Where No Man Has Gone Before", Charlie X, Roger Korby) that let audiences judge what makes someone human. It rejects the Cartesian reading (Richard Hanley's Is Data Human?) in which Data's humanity is just a matter of being a rational mind, and develops instead a feminist, developmental account of personhood drawn from Annette Baier: persons are "second persons" who learn the arts of personhood from caretakers. Data, Seven of Nine, and Voyager's Doctor, all lacking real childhoods and families, must learn play, touch, love, and interdependence from their crews, with Janeway modeling family for Seven and Kes socializing the Doctor. Picard's farewell to Shinzon in Nemesis and to Data's B-4 caps the claim that humanity is an achievement of self-improvement in relationship, not a fixed essence.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cogburn attacks Fourth Edition's contraction of the nine alignments to five: it deletes archetypes that fantasy literature needs, since Karsa Orlong (who wills the destruction of all civilization without sadism) and Jacqueline Carey's Haomane Firstborn (who loves cold mathematical order while his laws lead to genocide) fit nowhere in the new scheme. He rebuilds alignment by taking it to describe what a character wills in Kant's sense, mapping the law-chaos axis onto the categorical imperative (the liar and murderer must take themselves to be exceptions to universal laws) and the good-evil axis onto Mill's greatest happiness principle, which yields a Lawful Good of Gandhi and King, a Neutral Good modeled on Jesus breaking Sabbath law out of love, and Lawful Evil exemplified by vampire hierarchies and politicians whose policies create hell abroad. Joe Abercrombie's torturer San Dan Glotka becomes the archetypal Neutral Neutral, 'banality of evil' in Arendt's sense, and the chapter concludes Chaotic Good is empty because willing the destruction of universalizability cannot consistently will less pain.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Kraft uses Dunder Mifflin to test whether stockholder profit or stakeholder welfare should drive business decisions, introducing stakeholder theory via Ansoff and the Mitchell salience model. Michael's exclusive patronage of national chains (Chili's, Starbucks, USA Today) versus the staff's loyalty to local spots like Poor Richard's becomes a Millian case: by Mill's point that most good action benefits particular individuals, shopping locally spreads happiness through the Scranton community while Michael's habits export money and decision-making elsewhere. Dwight oscillates between stockholder logic (the cheapest health plan, poaching Jim's client in 'Diversity Day') and stakeholder-minded customer service, while 'Halloween,' 'Health Care,' and 'Branch Closing' show profit trumping people; Michael's successful sale to Christian at Chili's in 'The Client' balances both, and his 'Show me that farm' speech insists workers like Stanley and Phyllis are not replaceable cogs.

samples.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
samples.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
samples.relation: Southworth uses the War of Light to ask what role emotion should play in moral reasoning: Sinestro rules Korugar through fear, the Star Sapphires kidnap Sinestro Corps prisoners to convert them to love, Atrocitus's rage was forged by the Manhunters' massacre, Larfleeze hoards, and the Blue Lanterns merely hope that hope matters. On Aristotle's account every corps errs by excess: Atrocitus's rage makes him miss chances to kill Sinestro, Fatality's love benches John Stewart from saving his friends, and even the Green Lanterns' will-only ideal fails, since total fearlessness is itself vicious and Plato's picture has reason directing emotion like a general directing soldiers. He ends by defending Mill's utilitarianism: the Guardians' real failure was not detachment but pretending to be detached, and reading them as flawed 'benevolent, disinterested spectators' vindicates the Corps while explaining their moral growth after Scar and the Blackest Night.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: The Good Life and The Dexter-like Life
samples.relation: Abrol Fairweather uses Dexter as a controlled case study in the philosophy of emotion via Nozick's 'Spock Problem': like Spock, Dexter has beliefs, values and flawless practical reasoning but no emotional feelings, so Mill's Method of Difference lets us isolate what exactly emotions add. Distinguishing 'mere feelings' (beer on the boat, lust for Lila) from emotional feelings that run through our beliefs and values, he adopts Nozick's answer that emotions are value-perceptions - Dexter intellectually recognizes the value of Rita, Deb and his kids but cannot feel it, and that felt value is what his life lacks. Yet Dexter strikes back: he kills because he is too rational rather than too passionate, so whether the Dexter-like life beats the good life depends on whether emotions would help or hinder whatever matters most to us, a question the chapter briefly weighs in Millian terms of the balance of pleasure over pain his meta-killing produces.

samples.book: 070 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Raiding the Temple of Wisdom
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Cogburn protests Fourth Edition's contraction of the nine alignments and rebuilds the system philosophically: Lawful means willing universalizable law in Kant's categorical-imperative sense (the liar and murderer treating themselves as exceptions), Good means willing the greatest happiness in Mill's utilitarian sense, yielding a nine-box grid of moral psychologies. He populates it with fantasy archetypes—Haomane Firstborn as pathological Lawful Neutral, Karsa Orlong as Chaotic Neutral, Abercrombie's torturer Glotka as Neutral Neutral in Hannah Arendt's 'banality of evil' mold, hierarchic vampires and cynical politicians as Lawful Evil, Conan's raiders as Chaotic Evil. On this scheme Chaotic Good is genuinely empty, Drizzt and Robin Hood types are really Lawful or Neutral Good, and a Neutral Good versus Lawful Good dispute over killing one innocent to save thousands shows how gameplay can stage classic ethics thought experiments.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: John Henry, the Steam-Engine, and Folsom Prisoners
samples.relation: Mulnix pairs Cash with John Stuart Mill on the priority of quality of life over mere life: Mill's 1868 Parliament speech defends capital punishment as more humane than the "living tomb" of life imprisonment, and Cash agrees in the Folsom liner notes (the prisoner envying the cockroach that can leave) and in "The Mercy Seat," where the electric chair becomes both mercy and the throne of God. Mill's higher and lower pleasures, competent judges, and On Liberty's individuality illuminate Cash's gallery of fools, the "Folsom Prison Blues" narrator who shot a man just to watch him die, the mother-defying Billy Joe of "Don't Take Your Guns to Town," characters whose unreflective rebellion squanders rational freedom. John Henry, by contrast, exercised his higher faculties against the steam-engine and so died happy, proving the chapter's Millian thesis that freedom matters as a means to self-directed, deliberated happiness.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Murtagh asks whether the Virgin Mary statue spraying menstrual blood on a cardinal and the pope in 'Bloody Mary' is morally wrong, and answers with a utilitarian weighing of blasphemous humor's consequences. On the negative side, offense to believers (with Cartman's sudden piety about Family Guy's Muhammad in 'Cartoon Wars Part I' articulating the utilitarian worry that millions watching intensifies the harm) and a possible desensitizing erosion of tolerance; on the positive side, pleasure and the show's power to provoke thought, as when Randy learns from Stan that his five sober days came from his own willpower, not 'divine ass blood'. Drawing on Mill's greatest happiness principle and On Liberty's defense of open discussion, he concludes blasphemous humor is morally justified when it is an important part of a presentation with significant social value, and wrong when used merely to piss people off or for profit.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 5. Back from the Dead
samples.relation: Devlin and Cooper trace Rick's moral arc as a struggle between Mill-style consequentialism - twisted by the apocalypse into a 'Greatest Survival Principle' of mere survival (Dawn Lerner's Grady, Enid's 'JSS') - and Aristotelian virtue ethics. Shane's murder of Otis, the Governor's rule over Woodbury and killing of Martinez and Pete, and Terminus's cannibalism all show survival-only reasoning dissolving humanity, a decline the show underlines with literal mirror reflections of Shane as a walker. Rick falls after killing Shane and nearly trades Michonne to the Governor, is brought back by Lori's judging vision and the sight of Carl going cold, and reclaims virtues as habits grown like Hershel's seeds - 'We get to come back' (4.8 'Too Far Gone') - though Seasons 4 and 5 leave him balancing a harder character, down to 'We didn't want to waste the bullets,' with the drive to survive.

samples.book: 025 - The Beatles and Philosophy - Nothing You Can Think that Can't Be Thunk
samples.title: CHAPTER 1 “LET’S GET REAL, REAL GONE FOR A CHANGE”
samples.relation: The chapter argues that Elvis's Sun recordings — the staged rupture in 'Milkcow Blues Boogie' ('That don't move me. Let's get real, real gone for a change') and the accidental 'acting the fool' emergence of 'That's All Right' — enacted an epistemological revolution: a leap out of modernity's rationalized, disembodied mode into repressed bodily affect, defining American cool as affective authenticity against Bill Haley's affected performativity. Elvis's immersion in a Black Memphis neighborhood and his emulation of Black performers made him a catalyst for racial-musical integration and the 'visceral empathy' that prepared desegregation, while the panic of critics (Sinatra, the Times, Congressman Celler) is reread via Hegel's 'tarrying with the negative' as the resistance Geist needs for its self-overcoming. Creative novelty is described with Whitehead's and William James's metaphors — the 'lure of feeling,' sudden phase transition, radical empiricism in what Elvis kept or dropped onstage — with his 'did it make me feel good' studio criterion and a Zen-like mushin statesmanship of loosing egoic control in the band.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Funny Newspaper Makes Accurate Prophecy
samples.relation: Auxier takes the September 28, 2001 Onion issue—'Hijackers Surprised To Find Selves In Hell,' published while late-night TV was still in mourning—to ask what makes some comedy permissible and durable, glancing back at Aristophanes' caricature of Socrates in The Clouds and the circle-men speech Plato puts in his mouth in the Symposium. Hegel supplies the machinery: comedy as a moment of Art within Absolute Spirit may only bring to naught what is already null, while irony that diminishes the noble degrades the ironist—which is why the Warren Commission is fair game for 'Smithsonian Janitor Finds Magic Bullet' but Martin Luther King, a World Historical Individual whose individuality embodies his movement, can never anchor the 'Mrs. Williams Finally Decides Dinner Guest Is Not Going to Show' story. Since 'the news' itself is the great nullity—partial time-slices pretending to explain complex events before their meanings are interpretable—The Onion's rapid 9/11 satire was legitimate and even prophetic, deflating the bullshit of those posing as arbiters of Objective Spirit.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Obviously, the Borg Can’t Hold Their Liquor”
samples.relation: Decker asks 'What's it like to be a Borg?' and tests whether monist metaphysics justify the Collective: Parmenides's changeless, perfect Being matches the Borg's 'bringing them closer to perfection', Spinoza's one substance (God or Nature) makes assimilationist determinism intelligible and finds truth in Seven of Nine's nostalgia for collective harmony, and Hegel's teleological Geist — the whole 'the world, aware of itself' — most closely mirrors the Borg's galactic quest for an Omega-molecule perfection of 'infinite parts functioning as one.' Yet 'I, Borg' shows Hegelian Spirit working through individuals: Hugh's redemption transforms the Enterprise crew's self-understanding, proving nothing is wholly alien and freedom can coexist with collectivity. Via Haraway's cyborgs and against Kass's 'wisdom of repugnance', the chapter concludes the Borg horrify us because the natural/artificial dualism is already obsolete in our technologized lives — 'if we are the Borg, then resistance truly is futile.'

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Lawler charges that Gibson's atonement theology, in which the more barbaric the torture the greater the redemption, imprisons Christianity at the stage of Hegel's 'Unhappy Consciousness', where an infinite God is sundered from abject sinful humanity and a priestly mediator is needed. Reading the film through the master-slave dialectic (impotent master Pilate versus the dignified slave Simon of Cyrene; the world of separate egos as Hobbes's war of all against all), he argues that what dies on the cross is the separate ego itself, and that what rises is Geist, the 'I' that is 'We' of the loving human community. Against Tertullian's credo quia absurdum, and using Pascal's 'heart has its reasons' alongside Hegel's dialectical reason, he reads 'you are gods' and the prodigal son as teaching every person's essential divinity, so the film's own art (the Mater Dolorosa, our identification with the flesh-and-blood Jesus) implicitly undermines the separatist theology Gibson intends.

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 14. Things Can Happen that Nobody Could Imagine Only a Few Years Ago
samples.relation: Donna Marie Smith reads the series through Hegel's philosophy of history: the Crawleys' world is a clash of opposing forces - Lord Grantham's traditionalism against Matthew's and Branson's modernization, Violet's fear of electricity against Sybil's and Rose's embrace of the new - and this very conflict drives progress toward greater freedom. She uses Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right both to explain the entail and primogeniture that bar Mary from inheriting (the law preserves the 'house' over the immediate family, which Hegel calls an infringement of the freedom of property) and to frame Robert's refusal to challenge it as duty to his social standing outweighing personal wishes. WWI, which Hegel experienced through Napoleon's occupation of Jena, is presented as a 'march toward freedom' that breaks down class barriers and finally pushes Robert to accept change on the estate: 'Let's give it a go and see what the future brings.'

samples.book: 095 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - Thinking in That Manor
samples.title: 14. Things Can Happen that Nobody Could Imagine Only a Few Years Ago
samples.relation: Donna Marie Smith reads the series as a Hegelian drama in which the opposing forces of tradition and progress - Lord Grantham, Carson, and Violet defending the old estate world against Matthew, Sybil, and Tom Branson embracing new ideas - drive history as 'the progress of the consciousness of freedom.' Using Hegel's Elements of the Philosophy of Right, she explains why Robert treats upholding the entail against the protests of Mary, Cora, and even Violet as his duty as custodian, while noting Hegel's own objection that such inheritance law gives family members like the Crawley women 'no right to recognition.' The war announced at the season 1 garden party is read through Hegel's experience of Napoleon at Jena and his view that war can advance Geist, and the chapter closes with telephones, electric mixers, Sybil's marriage, and Isobel Crawley concluding that tradition and change can finally coexist.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: The Force of Love
samples.relation: Lawler identifies Hegel's Absolute Spirit with the Force: Hegel's distillation of religious history - divine nature (the Ewoks worshipping C-3PO), the Roman Empire's transcendent Unhappy Consciousness, and Christianity's Consummate Religion - maps onto the saga's movement, with Anakin's virgin birth, prophecy, fall, and Calvary-like redemption fulfilling the pattern differently from the sinless Savior. The Dark Side is the separate ego asserting 'I' against 'We' (Hobbes's war of all against all culminating in the Emperor), and sin is the belief that one is an isolated individual. samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Argues that a motorcycle club is a Machiavellian regime in miniature: Jax's Season 3 fake betrayal of the club to Stahl—actually a set-up that shortens the crew's prison time and delivers both Stahl and Jimmy O to death—shows the prince's union of lion and fox in service of the club rather than himself. samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: Goals for All Ages and All Occasions
samples.relation: Opening with Camus's line that crushing truths perish from being acknowledged (and his Sisyphus, invoked to show the intrinsically interested player always wins), the authors force football to face its ugly side—divers, Pepe kicking Casquero on the ground, Catania's mooning free-kick screen, referee Pérez Burrull's robbery of Osasuna, the Heysel disaster, Bilardo pinning opponents and drugging Branco, FIFA's resistance to technology—analyzing it all with MacIntyre's account of social practices: football's constitutive rules and internal goods generate standards of excellence that cheating betrays for extrinsic rewards. Their positive ideal is the Greek Kalon, the noble-and-beautiful they field for Plato and Aristotle, exemplified when De Rossi confesses his handball goal against Messina or opponents return the ball after an injury stoppage—the beau geste uniting aesthetic grace and moral honor, as in the 4–4 Arsenal–Liverpool classic where 'neither side deserved to lose'. samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness

samples.title: America’s Game
samples.relation: William Morgan answers Richard Rorty's charge that American pop culture breeds only militaristic chauvinism by pointing to baseball's moral self-story: played for love of the game (Whitman) rather than market value. samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Abigail Mann argues that the Games only look like 'survival of the fittest': Darwinian natural selection runs on chance ('one slip in thousands') and explicitly rejects the social-Darwinist use of 'unfit' against the poor, while Darwin's Descent of Man explains the tributes' kindness through kin and group selection and an evolved moral sense, so Katniss's unhesitating volunteering for Prim is kin selection and Thresh's conflicted sparing of her shows conscience overriding self-preservation. Her coda: Katniss ultimately rejects Gale not only because his firebomb killed Prim but because it was engineered to trap and kill altruists, and her closing habit of listing 'every act of goodness' is the trilogy's verdict that simple kindness is not an illusion.

samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Robert Arp's gallery matches each Gang vice - dishonesty, egoism, selfishness, greed, pettiness, ignorance, laziness - to real-life scumbags from Nixon, Stephen Glass, and Janet Cooke to Charles Ponzi, Bernie Madoff, Crassus, the Empress Dowager Cixi, Imelda Marcos, and the Darwin Awards, and it opens with the chapter's philosophical spine: Glaucon's Ring of Gyges from Book II of Plato's Republic, which predicts that even an upstanding person with the power to act unseen would seduce, steal, and murder - exactly the question the Gang's mostly unpunished antics keep staging. samples.title: The Universe Is Not Indifferent

samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Uses 'Fun with Veal' (the boys' bedroom standoff over baby calves, the FDA renaming veal 'tortured baby cows', Stan's meat strike punished by 'vaginitus'), 'Whale Whores' (the Japanese hating dolphins until Stan's doctored Enola Gay photo swaps in a cow and chicken), and 'Pee' (researchers peeing on rhesus monkeys) to pose the line-drawing problem: why do we protect cute animals and slaughter yummy ones? samples.title: Gay Angels, Female Cardinals, and Bishōnen Popes

Because Shinto-Buddhist-Daoist anti-realism dissolves fixed categories, anime dissolves good and evil (Chrno Crusade's I Ching balance) and gender itself, gravitating to the symbol-rich 'jungle' of Catholicism (C.S. Lewis's phrase) — and where Trinity Blood lets some vampires be righteous, Augustine's City of God marks the one nearly orthodox note.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: So Why Do I Support Aston Villa
samples.relation: Rose—made a Villan by misreading a 1978 Panini sticker as Aston Villa's claret and blue—asks whether supporting Aston Villa is rational and argues ethics is far more like fandom than philosophers admit. Reasons for supporting Villa (local team, the 1982 European Cup, the colors) explain but never justify his allegiance, and the impartial procedures ethics prizes—the utilitarian benevolent spectator and Rawls's original position behind the veil of ignorance, with its 'sort of Kantian' consent-based alternative—turn out too demanding and too abstract: they would force him to donate his match ticket to charity, forbid the Premiership manager favoring his academy son, and reduce agency to the 'Rose-calcio scale' absurdity of switching to Real Madrid for rational reasons. samples.title: Where Do We Go from Here
samples.relation: David Kyle Johnson argues that Colbert's gut-thinking persona (the Harriet Miers 'I know her heart' bit, 'that's my right' on the Panama Canal) satirizes a real and widespread vice, and he refutes the philosophies behind it. Against this he holds up Socrates, wisest because he alone admitted ignorance, and insists philosophy and politics progress only through argument, so truthiness is never an acceptable substitute.

samples.title: If Not on the Island of Ethical Subjectivism, Then Where

He concludes that Lost's ambiguous cases - Michael's murder of Ana Lucia and Libby, Ben killing Jacob, Jack extorting Ben on the operating table - invite viewers to seek objective grounds Socratically, questioning their own moral judgments with further 'why's.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: King weighs whether Victor or his creation bears the blame, opening with a thought experiment in which a neighbor's self-aware android burns your town and asking 'does he deserve to share that fate?' Maslow's hierarchy of needs explains the monster's fixation on a mate as a starved 'love need' created by Victor's abandonment, and Piaget's cognitive stages test whether the monster had matured enough to 'could have done otherwise' - while Nietzsche's Beyond Good and Evil attack on morality as tyrannical herd-style slave morality threatens to dissolve blame entirely, and Sartre's existentialism leaves each agent choosing without objective moral foundations. Refusing both the absolutist's unconditional verdict and dogmatic relativism, the chapter applies the criminal law's mens rea ('guilty mind') test to monster, android, and creator alike, and leaves the final verdict of guilt deliberately open.

samples.title: Questioning the Question
samples.relation: Hartung takes Ross's snapping reply to Armitage's repeated 'Why are you helping me?' in Armitage the Third: Poly-Matrix as a misreading: she wants a practical reason for his choice, not theoretical evidence, and since no evidence can prove an android is a person, William James's 'Will to Believe' applies — Ross's belief in her moral standing is a live, forced, and momentous genuine option (suspending judgment means she is scrapped, and losing her means losing a possible life together), so his passions may legitimately decide. samples.book: 163 - Game of Thrones and Philosophy - Logic Cuts Deeper Than Swords
samples.title: Game of Thrones and Philosophy
samples.relation: Eric Silverman argues Game of Thrones explodes the storybook link between virtue and worldly happiness: Ned, 'one man in ten thousand,' is betrayed and executed, so Plato's claim that the just person is happy must mean psychic order rather than material flourishing - reason ruling spirit and appetite - as with Bran, who flourishes as a greenseer though he will never walk again. Cersei is Plato's tyrant, her soul ruled by insatiable appetite and paranoia, so no external goods can ever satisfy her, while Aristotle's correction - virtue necessary but not sufficient for eudaimonia, which also needs health, friends, and good fortune - explains why both Ned (virtue without external goods) and Cersei (goods without virtue) end up unhappy. Finally he inverts Pascal's Wager: since playing the game of thrones risks total loss (torture, humiliation, death) for limited gain, and even winning hollows you out - Robert confesses he was 'never so alive as when I was winning this throne or so dead as now that I've won it' - only a fool would play.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 9. With Infinite Power Comes No Responsibility
samples.relation: James Hart casts Tony Stark as a consequentialist and Steve Rogers as a deontologist, then argues Endgame's infinite stakes destroy Tony's morality through Nick Bostrom's 'infinitarian paralysis': in an infinite multiverse every act leaves the balance of happy and sad lives unchanged, as an infinite Stark orphanage rearranged Hilbert's-Hotel style shows, and even genocide becomes permissible so long as infinitely many remain alive. Tony's attempted fixes each fail: the causal approach collapses because reversing the Snap has infinite butterfly effects, expected value (credited to Frank Jackson) runs into Pascal's Mugging and an 'infinitarian trance' demanding suicidal bets on any chance of infinite value, and Bostrom's 'infinity shades' that filter tiny probabilities would blind Tony to the one-in-a-trillion time-heist chance he should take. The chapter concludes there is no consequentialist way to say when wagering lives on infinite stakes is ethical, and Iron Man should let Captain America lead.
